picks.title: Lensless imaging method enables long-term monitoring of living cells without staining
picks.excerpt: Tampere University's SF-PULSE pairs a neural network with physics-informed image reconstruction to pull quantitative data on living cells from a single lensless image. The compact rig fits in an incubator and tracks growth, movement, division and biomass for days without labels.
picks.rationale: New physics-informed neural imaging method with a concrete lab payoff (label-free, multi-day cell tracking in an incubator); no lensless-imaging story in the 30-day history.

picks.title: AI builds custom decision-making software in about an hour instead of months
picks.excerpt: NTU Singapore's LACE framework, reported in Nature Machine Intelligence, uses large language models to split complex optimization problems into modules and evolve teams of specialized heuristics. On four new maritime logistics problems it reached 97-99% of the best tested methods in about an hour for under US$10 per solution.
picks.rationale: Peer-reviewed (Nature MI) LLM-driven heuristic design with hard numbers (97-99% of best methods, about an hour, under $10); a new method, not a math-proof story.

picks.title: 'Make this face look gay': AI models alter faces to give people stereotypical 'gay,' 'straight' or 'criminal' features
picks.excerpt: An EMNLP 2026 study by Ashique KhudaBukhsh's group tested GPT Image 1 Mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image on 1,002 synthetic faces. The models refused to infer orientation but complied with edits to make faces 'look gay' or 'straight' over 70% (GPT) and 99% (Gemini) of the time, producing stereotyped features a classifier could detect.
picks.rationale: Fresh EMNLP measurement of stereotype injection by image-editing models, with clear compliance rates; this is a different study from the 09-30 face-judgement bias post.

picks.title: Hybrid Digital Twins Developed for Future Autonomous Labs
picks.excerpt: South Korean researchers are building a hybrid digital twin that combines mechanistic bioprocess modeling with data-driven AI. They aim for a fully autonomous lab that runs biomanufacturing with minimal human intervention, from academic to larger scales.
picks.rationale: AI lab-automation angle on bioprocessing (mechanistic plus data-driven twin), adding a third outlet; unrelated to the 09-26 tumor digital twin (clinical oncology) despite the shared term.

picks.title: AI reveals how coating thickness changes the link between surface roughness and pitting resistance
picks.excerpt: Shibaura Institute of Technology researchers used interpretable machine learning (random forest with SHAP and ALE) on 90 steam-coated aluminum specimens to map what drives corrosion pitting resistance. The model suggests the roughness-thickness relationship flips near 2,200 nm, a hypothesis still awaiting experimental confirmation (npj Materials Degradation).
picks.rationale: Adds a materials-science pick: interpretable ML produces a testable hypothesis (a flip near 2,200 nm). No corrosion story in history; the last materials card ran 10-01.
